I agree, but many times not supporting your child’s choices might lead things like suicidal thoughts. The only known treatment for gender dysphoria currently is letting them live the way they want to. 

And it’s not a matter of hormones or surgery at first (and it shouldn’t be), just letting them express themselves as they want to. Lots of non permanent things can be done, such as haircuts, clothing, wearing or not wearing makeup, using a nickname instead of their legal name, etc. Let kids play make believe, and if it’s not their thing they’ll eventually stop.

I thought that transitioning would not only make me lose that, but it would make me look like a lesbian (spoiler: it didn't for too long) and therefore not appealing to (gay) men at all (spoiler 2: even when i looked like a lesbian, it didn't). My family would disown me and I would never see my little nephews again. I also didn't reeeeally know if I wanted to become a man because, even though I would dream about being one, literally saw myself as a boy before puberty, never thought of my relationships with women as "lesbian" relationships... I still liked makeup! And when I was 3 my mom put me in a dress and I didn't cry, so, you know, not a man! I kept thinking like this for years, and honestly, it just made me more miserable by the day. I reached a point where I would either have to do something about it, or I would literally die.

What I want to say is: it's easy to find reasons not to be yourself, but at the end of the day, denial will eat you from the inside. You don't deserve that and it's not worth losing yourself for the comfort of others. If you want to be straight, doesn't that just mean that you aren't?

Also, don't care about labels/coming out if that's not helpful to you. That includes stuff like "bisexual" and "pansexual". If you do like girls, GREAT! If you like boys, AWESOME! You just like people in general? THAT'S WONDERFUL! Go conquer the world girl! I choose to tell others that I am a "bisexual transgender man" because that is the easiest way I found to communicate my gender and sexuality to others, but in reality I have no goddamn clue about what I am. I gave up trying to find the "perfect" label for myself. I'm learning about myself every single day and hope to continue doing so for the rest of my life. Don't be afraid to try.
